---
title: "Question 2 - LDA Topic Modelling of News Articles"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6)
```

## Packages and parameters

```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("tidyverse","tidytext","topicmodels","textstem","wordcloud","RColorBrewer","reshape2","ldatuning"))
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(topicmodels)
library(textstem)
library(wordcloud)
library(RColorBrewer)

N_TOPICS <- 5     # n: number of topics
K_WORDS  <- 10    # k: top words shown per topic
set.seed(1234)
```

## 2.1 Load the news files into a data frame and denoise

```{r load}
zip_path <- "news.zip"                 # place news.zip next to this notebook
unzip(zip_path, exdir = "news_raw")

files <- list.files("news_raw", pattern = "\\.txt$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

news_df <- tibble(
  file_name = basename(files),
  content   = map_chr(files, ~ paste(readLines(.x, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = " "))
)

glimpse(news_df)
```

Denoising steps: strip HTML tags and URLs, lower-case, remove digits and punctuation, collapse whitespace, remove stop words and very short tokens, lemmatise.

```{r clean}
clean_text <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") |>           # HTML
    str_replace_all("http\\S+|www\\.\\S+", " ") |> # URLs
    str_replace_all("\\S+@\\S+", " ") |>         # e-mails
    str_to_lower() |>
    str_replace_all("[^a-z\\s]", " ") |>         # punctuation, digits, symbols
    str_squish()
}

news_df <- news_df |> mutate(clean = clean_text(content))

extra_stop <- c("said","say","says","will","also","would","could","one","two","new","year","years","mr","mrs")

tokens <- news_df |>
  select(file_name, clean) |>
  unnest_tokens(word, clean) |>
  filter(!word %in% stop_words$word,
         !word %in% extra_stop,
         nchar(word) > 2) |>
  mutate(word = lemmatize_words(word))

# lemmatising can reintroduce stop words, so filter again
tokens <- tokens |> filter(!word %in% stop_words$word)

# remove very rare words (< 3 occurrences overall)
tokens <- tokens |> group_by(word) |> filter(n() >= 3) |> ungroup()

# preprocessed data frame (file_name, content)
news_clean <- tokens |>
  group_by(file_name) |>
  summarise(content = paste(word, collapse = " "), .groups = "drop")

head(news_clean)
cat("Documents:", nrow(news_clean), " Vocabulary:", n_distinct(tokens$word), "\n")
```

## 2.2 LDA

Document-term matrix and model:

```{r lda}
dtm <- tokens |>
  count(file_name, word) |>
  cast_dtm(file_name, word, n)

lda_model <- LDA(dtm, k = N_TOPICS, method = "Gibbs",
                 control = list(seed = 1234, burnin = 500, iter = 2000))
```

Top k words per topic (beta = probability of the word given the topic, i.e. the word distribution):

```{r topwords}
topic_words <- tidy(lda_model, matrix = "beta")

top_terms <- topic_words |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(beta, n = K_WORDS, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(topic, desc(beta))

top_terms

# compact list view
top_terms |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  summarise(top_words = paste(term, collapse = ", "))
```

Word distribution reporting: how concentrated each topic is, and how topics spread over documents.

```{r dist}
# share of each topic's probability mass held by its top k words
topic_words |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  arrange(desc(beta), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(top_k_mass = sum(head(beta, K_WORDS)), vocab = n())

# document-topic distribution (gamma) and dominant topic per document
doc_topics <- tidy(lda_model, matrix = "gamma")

dominant <- doc_topics |>
  group_by(document) |>
  slice_max(gamma, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

count(dominant, topic, name = "documents")
```

(Optional) choosing n with coherence-style metrics:

```{r choose-n, eval=FALSE}
library(ldatuning)
res <- FindTopicsNumber(dtm, topics = seq(2, 12, 2),
        metrics = c("Griffiths2004","CaoJuan2009","Arun2010","Deveaud2014"),
        method = "Gibbs", control = list(seed = 1234), mc.cores = 2L)
FindTopicsNumber_plot(res)
```

## 2.3 Visualisation

**Method 1 - faceted bar chart of top words per topic**

```{r bars}
top_terms |>
  mutate(term = reorder_within(term, beta, topic)) |>
  ggplot(aes(beta, term, fill = factor(topic))) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Topic", topic), scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  labs(title = "Top words per topic (LDA)",
       x = "Word probability within topic (beta)", y = "Word")
```

**Method 2 - word clouds per topic**

```{r clouds, fig.height=8}
par(mfrow = c(ceiling(N_TOPICS / 2), 2), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (t in seq_len(N_TOPICS)) {
  d <- filter(top_terms, topic == t)
  wordcloud(d$term, d$beta, scale = c(3, 0.6), min.freq = 0,
            colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"), random.order = FALSE)
  title(paste("Topic", t))
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Method 3 (bonus) - document-topic heatmap**

```{r heat}
ggplot(doc_topics, aes(factor(topic), document, fill = gamma)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(title = "Topic proportions per document", x = "Topic", y = "Document", fill = "Gamma") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
```

## Interpretation

Write 1-2 sentences per topic naming it from its top words (e.g. "Topic 1: politics and elections"), comment on how concentrated each topic is (top_k_mass), and on how many documents each topic dominates.
